This guide follows a complete hierarchical-model analysis of the included
deep vein thrombosis data, from installation to posterior summaries and plots.
The figures and numerical output below were generated with NMADTA 0.1.4.

## Installation

NMADTA needs **R 4.0.0 or later** and **JAGS 4.x**. JAGS is a separate program:
install it from the [JAGS project](https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io/) first.

~~~r
install.packages("NMADTA")
library(NMADTA)
rjags::jags.version()
packageVersion("NMADTA")
~~~

If `rjags` cannot load, check that JAGS is installed for your operating system
and processor architecture, then restart R.

## Inspect the study data

The `dat.kang` dataset has 48 rows of joint outcome counts from 12 studies.
The candidate tests are D-dimer and ultrasonography; venography is the reference.

| Tests observed | Studies |
|:--|--:|
| D-dimer and venography | 4 |
| Ultrasonography and venography | 3 |
| D-dimer and ultrasonography | 5 |

~~~r
data(dat.kang)
head(dat.kang)
~~~

~~~
  sid delta0 delta1 delta2 T0 T1  T2  n
1   1      1      1      0  1  1 999 16
2   1      1      1      0  1  0 999  5
3   1      1      1      0  0  1 999  4
4   1      1      1      0  0  0 999 28
5   2      1      1      0  1  1 999 32
6   2      1      1      0  1  0 999  5
~~~

A missing test is indicated by `delta = 0` and the outcome code `999`.
These rows record joint test outcomes, rather than a separate 2 by 2 table
for every comparison. Read [Preparing your data](data-format.html) before
using your own study data.

## Fit the hierarchical model

Here `nstu = 12` is the number of studies and `K = 2` counts the candidate
tests, excluding the reference standard.

~~~r
set.seed(10)
kang_fit <- nmadt.hierarchical(
  nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,
  testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),
  directory = tempdir(),
  n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3,
  n.burnin = 25000, n.thin = 1,
  conv.diag = TRUE, trace = NULL,
  dic = FALSE, mcmc.samples = FALSE
)
~~~

This run uses 5,000 adaptation iterations, followed by 50,000 iterations per
chain, with the first 25,000 removed as burn-in. Three chains are used.
Running time depends on the model, data, and computer.

## Read the posterior summaries

~~~r
summary(kang_fit)
~~~

~~~
Model: hierarchical 

Sensitivity (Median and 95% CrI):
                Median (95% CI)        
D-dimer         0.8513 (0.6928, 0.9783)
Ultrasonography 0.9310 (0.8265, 0.9924)

Specificity (Median and 95% CrI):
                Median (95% CI)        
D-dimer         0.8721 (0.7191, 0.9878)
Ultrasonography 0.7640 (0.4833, 0.9638)
~~~

These are the sensitivity and specificity summaries from this run.
The full output also includes prevalence, predictive values, and likelihood
ratios. Download the [complete summary](../example/summary.txt).
Numerical results can vary across platforms and JAGS runs.

## Visualize diagnostic accuracy

~~~r
plot(kang_fit, type = "sroc")
~~~

![NMADTA SROC output for the D-dimer and ultrasonography example.](../figures/example-sroc.png)

The first two panels show the SROC display for each candidate test. The third
compares the fitted curves and study-level estimates.

~~~r
plot(kang_fit, type = "forest")
~~~

![NMADTA forest plots of study-level sensitivity and specificity for the two candidate tests.](../figures/example-forest.png)

Points mark study-level posterior medians and horizontal intervals show 95%
credible intervals. Vertical dotted lines mark the pooled posterior medians.
Dashed horizontal intervals identify studies in which that candidate test was
not observed; these estimates are model-based.

Other available displays are `type = "density"` and `type = "contour"`.
See [`plot.nmadt()`](../reference/plot.nmadt.html) for options.

## Assess convergence and assumptions

The fit requests potential scale reduction factors through `conv.diag = TRUE`.
A writable `directory` is required for these diagnostics or trace files.
To inspect trace plots, fit the model with a selected quantity such as
`trace = "Se"` or `trace = "Sp"`.

In this illustrative run, the largest PSRF point estimate was 1.27 for the
positive likelihood ratio of ultrasonography. Extend the run and reassess
diagnostics before substantive inference for that quantity.

Check mixing, convergence, and sensitivity to prior choices before interpreting
results. Longer chains may be needed. To retain the additional MCMC sample
output, use `mcmc.samples = TRUE`.

The regular function uses the MAR formulation. Use dedicated
[MNAR functions](missing-data.html) to examine alternative missing-data
assumptions.
